🇲🇽💵 <u>Remittances to Mexico rose again in July — $5.57 billion, six straight months up</u>

Banxico reports Mexican families received $5,571 million dollars in July, up 3% year-on-year and a sixth consecutive monthly increase, for $36.35 billion in the first seven months of 2026 (+3.1%), per El Financiero. It came from 13.1 million transactions averaging $426 each — and it held up despite Washington's aggressive deportation drive, with the very migrants the US targets sending more money home than a year ago.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>Mexican forces dismantle 3 meth superlabs in Guerrero — even Washington's ambassador took notice</u>

Federal forces knocked out three methamphetamine labs in Guerrero, seizing tons of precursor chemicals and dozens of industrial-scale tanks in simultaneous raids. US Ambassador Ronald Johnson called it "otro ejemplo de lo que podemos lograr cuando nuestros países comparten información y se coordinan" — worth remembering that those precursors ship in from abroad, and the labs were taken down on Mexican soil by Mexican forces. Cooperation, not subordination.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Two ex-admirals ran one of Mexico's biggest fuel-smuggling networks, FGR confirms</u>

Attorney General Ernestina Godoy confirmed that brothers Roberto and Fernando Farías Laguna — both retired navy admirals — headed a "huachicol fiscal" operation moving fuel out of Texas mislabeled as "oil or additives" to dodge taxes, with 10 million liters of diesel seized from a single ship in Altamira and cells across five states. "Quien haya usado un uniforme, cargo público o aduana para servir al crimen, debe responder ante la justicia," she said. The case broke from an internal navy complaint — the institution turning on its own corruption.

🇲🇽💜 <u>42 million Mexicans now receive a pension or welfare program — over 1 trillion pesos a year</u>

Bienestar Secretary Leticia Ramírez Amaya put it plainly: "La riqueza de México debe traducirse en bienestar para el pueblo." 42 million people are covered — 13 million elderly on the universal pension alone (6,400 pesos every two months), plus women aged 60-64, people with disabilities, and 445,000 farmers under Sembrando Vida. This is what the 1 trillion pesos the opposition dismisses as "populism" actually buys.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Televisa just had its worst day on the stock market in 25 years</u>

Grupo Televisa — the old regime's propaganda machine — plunged as much as 14.3% Monday, its worst session since 2001, after S&P said it will drop the company from Mexico's benchmark S&P/BMV IPC index. After 35 years in the country's elite index it gets replaced by Alpek, sinking to 7.60 pesos, its lowest price since July 2025. The change is confirmed Sept 11 and takes effect Sept 21.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexico's 2027 budget: no new taxes — they're coming for the tax cheats instead</u>

Sheinbaum sends the 2027 economic package to Congress with a flat promise: "No ha habido un aumento de impuestos ni va a haber." No new taxes, no VAT hike — instead Hacienda goes after the "factureras," the fake-invoice mills that drain roughly 1.45 trillion pesos a year from the treasury. That recovered money funds the same 1 trillion+ pesos in pensions and scholarships the opposition swore was unaffordable.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO NOW EXPORTS MORE TECH THAN CARS</u>

For the first time in decades, cars aren't Mexico's top export. AI infrastructure — servers, boards, the guts of the data-center boom — hit 163 billion dollars over 12 months, up 148% year-on-year, surpassing the entire auto sector, El Financiero reports citing UBS. The nearshoring everyone predicted showed up as a 20 billion dollar tech trade surplus.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SALINAS PLIEGO FUNDED AN IMPORTED DISINFO MACHINE</u>

Fernando Cerimedo — the far-right operative behind Latin America's disinformation networks, now arrested in Bolivia — built "La Derecha Diario" in Mexico by invitation of billionaire Ricardo Salinas Pliego, using tech from Trump's ex-digital chief Brad Parscale, with 132.8 million dollars traced in his crypto wallets. The stated mission, boasted at CPAC: interfering in Mexico's 2027 elections.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>VULCAN WANTED $1.7 BILLION. MEXICO WANTS ITS LAND BACK</u>

US mining giant Vulcan Materials gouged Quintana Roo's coast until AMLO turned the over-extracted site into a protected natural area. The ICSID tribunal just ruled its payout should land far below the $1.7 billion Vulcan demanded. Sheinbaum's line in the talks: "They want to take out the material they already dug up. What we want is the remediation of that place."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>MEXICO'S NEW COURT ENDS ITS OWN PERKS</u>

The elected Supreme Court just cancelled the luxuries the old one guarded: major-medical insurance for justices, separation payouts, and superfluous services, plus a 10% cut to administrative staff — part of over 4.7 billion pesos in judicial savings this year. Court president Hugo Aguilar Ortiz, the first Indigenous man to hold the post: "The privileges are over."
